text:
kevin: Quick question — we need to pick a default transport for control-plane/internal APIs that power the Console (routing policy edits, quota checks, rollout signals). REST (JSON) at the gateway vs gRPC/Protobuf between services. Thoughts?

maria: strong +1 for gRPC for service-to-service. typed contracts, smaller wire, streaming is useful for rollout status updates.

jen: :thinking_face: I like types but console engineers will want curlability and simple network debugging. REST is easier for ad-hoc queries and debugging dashboards.

sam: can we do a hybrid? internal mesh uses gRPC/proto. edge/gateway does REST <-> gRPC transcoding for browser and external clients. that keeps internal correctness and external ergonomics.

kevin: hybrid seems reasonable. two immediate pain points: 1) telemetry/trace/attr propagation through transcoding; 2) per-route quota & cost attribution when gateway normalizes requests.

maria: agreed. tracing headers often get lost when envoy does transcoding. need explicit header passthrough + span tagging at gateway. also watch for proto enums -> string mapping in logs.

jen: for quotas the console wants token-level breakdowns in the UI (per route/model). If gateway folds multiple internal RPCs into one HTTP request, we need a way to attribute costs back to routes. maybe gateway emits "x-internal-ops" header with op IDs and token counts.

sam: quick POC suggestion — use envoy + grpc-web for browser, enable grpc_transcoding filter to accept JSON and forward typed proto. sample envoy route snippet: 
```
- match: 
    prefix: "/api/v1/"
  route: 
    cluster: control-plane
  typed_per_filter_config: 
    envoy.filters.http.grpc_json_transcoder: 
      proto_descriptor: "/etc/protos/control.pb"
      services: ["control.ControlService"]
```
This keeps proto contracts internal while still receiving JSON from the console.

kevin: nice. any concerns about payload bloat or perf if we do JSON<->proto work at gateway?

maria: CPU cost is non-trivial but still cheaper than shipping heavier RPCs. we should benchmark with typical Console payload shapes (policy blobs, rollout lists). also consider streaming side-channel: e.g., console subscribes to rollout updates via websocket/grpc-web, not long-poll REST.

jen: on debuggability, we should add a transient endpoint on the control-plane that returns a prettified proto JSON for a given op id. e.g., `GET /debug/op/{id}` that forwards internally to the gRPC method and prints proto JSON. helps SREs and PMs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Reminder — canary for the gateway transcoding node pool is scheduled for 03/30 02:00 UTC. Label: canary/grpc-transcode. :rotating_light:

sam: action items I hear: 1) build small envoy grpc_transcoding POC, 2) run telemetry propagation tests (traces + custom headers), 3) add quota attribution header proposal, 4) perf bench for JSON<->proto cost. I'll spin up the POC this week.

kevin: thanks — sounds good. I'll draft an RFC (hybrid-transport-for-console.md) outlining the pattern, including sample configs and the attribution header spec. tagging @maria @jen for review.

maria: will review. also add tests for enum/string conversions so dashboards don't flip when we change proto schemas.

jen: also add a small UX note: console should surface "approx cost impact" when editing routing/quotas so product folks can see immediate effect.

kevin: great. last note — keep the default for internal services as gRPC unless a service owns an explicit REST facade. we'll capture exceptions in the RFC.

sam: ok I'll drop the first POC branch and ping this thread.

kevin: thanks everyone.
